subject: Clarify order form ownership & escrow pass-through — CloudCart marketplace
messages:
From: Susan Tan <susan.tan@cloudcart.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace order form questions and redlines (attached)
Cc: CloudCart Legal <legal@cloudcart.com>

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the discussion yesterday. We pulled together an initial redline of the order form for the CloudCart listing (attached: CloudCart_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx). Two items we need clarified from Redwood before we can proceed with procurement:

1) Order form ownership: CloudCart is pushing for the seller (CloudCart) to remain the contracting party for the order form on marketplace listings. Redwood sales mentioned there is a pass-through option — can you confirm who will be the contracting party on the face of the order form and whether Redwood requires an MSA amendment for this?

2) Pass-through liability and escrow: procurement needs to understand whether pass-through charges (fees, taxes, refunds) are eligible for escrow and whether Redwood will accept upstream liability carveouts. Attached is a simple matrix of the expected flows.

We have a legal touchpoint Thursday and would like to understand Redwood's preferred language so we don't rework redlines multiple times. Are you able to propose language for: (a) order form ownership block, (b) a pass-through fee carveout that limits Redwood liability to service delivery only?

Attachments: CloudCart_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx (redline), prod_pass_through_matrix.xlsx (routing)

Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful — we have availability 7/15 AM PST.

Best,
Susan
Director, Commercial Partnerships
CloudCart

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Susan Tan <susan.tan@cloudcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace order form questions and redlines (attached)

Hi Susan —

Thanks for sending these over and for the clear matrix. Looping in Ben (partner ops), Karthik (legal) and Olga (billing ops) so we can get aligned internally and provide suggested language by EOD. Quick notes up front:

- We typically allow two patterns for marketplace listings: (1) Redwood as reseller (Redwood contracts with buyer; seller faciliates through a partner paper), or (2) pass-through where seller remains the contracting party and Redwood acts as a conduit for payment/fulfillment.
- Pass-through is feasible but we need to nail down the liability carveouts and payment routing in the order form; procurement will want explicit language for escrow and auditing.

I can set a 30-min call for 7/15 9:00 AM PST — does that work for your team? If so, I'll send a calendar invite. For the redline, Karthik will propose MSA/order form language that preserves Redwood's SLA/backstop while allowing seller-led contracting on the face of the order form.

Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Marketplace order form questions and redlines (attached)

Laura / team —

Forwarding CloudCart's notes. High-level ops perspective:

- Order form ownership: CloudCart's ask to remain the contracting party is fine from an onboarding standpoint, but we need clarity on invoicing and refund flow. If CloudCart signs the order form, they will be responsible for tax withholdings and chargebacks in most regions. We should require a written delegation of billing authority or an escrow flow that names Redwood as a payee in fallback scenarios.

- Escrow/pass-through: We should accept pass-through for subscription fees and taxes, but require a carveback for chargebacks and fraud where Redwood is required to refund customers directly because of platform issues. We'll surface the exact fallback wording.

I've attached a quick "prod_pass_through_matrix.xlsx" with how our billing engine expects fields. Olga, can you confirm whether our preview invoicing pipeline supports seller-owned order forms and what the admin UX will look like?

Attachments: prod_pass_through_matrix.xlsx

Ben Carter
Partner Operations, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 17:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace order form questions and redlines (attached)

Team —

Quick legal read and proposed language snippets below (I pulled CloudCart's attached redline into the doc as well). High level: Redwood can support seller-owned order forms with pass-through fees, subject to three constraints:

1) Indemnity/responsibility carveouts: We cannot accept broad carveouts that shift product liability or regulatory obligations entirely to Redwood's partners. Proposed snippet: "Partner shall remain the contracting party vis-à-vis the Buyer. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood shall retain primary responsibility for service-level obligations provided through the Redwood platform; Partner's liability shall be limited to amounts actually collected from Buyer and passed through to Redwood. Neither Party may disclaim liability for gross negligence or willful misconduct."

2) Escrow/audit rights: Procurement must be able to trigger an audit. Proposed: "Payment pass-through amounts shall be subject to audit upon reasonable notice. Escrow arrangements shall name Redwood as contingent payee in the event Partner becomes insolvent or is otherwise unable to remit funds due for services delivered by Redwood."

3) Order form signature matrix and fallback: If Partner signs the order form, we need a counterparty delegation that authorizes Redwood to chargebacks/refunds in defined circumstances. Proposed fallback clause: "If Partner fails to remit required refunds or tax withholdings within 30 days following a final determination, Redwood reserves the right to withhold future disbursements and to set off amounts against Partner payouts."

Next steps: I will produce an annotated redline of CloudCart_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx with inline suggestions and a short comment summary. Laura — suggest we provide CloudCart with (A) a targeted order form redline and (B) an MSA addendum paragraph that references 'marketplace pass-through' and the escrow fallback. Olga — once Karthik posts the redline, can you confirm the backend implications for payouts and whether we need a new reconciliation field?

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace order form questions and redlines (attached)

Laura / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. We reviewed Karthik's summary with procurement and legal: we can accept the proposed order form ownership language provided two small adjustments:

1) Escrow naming: instead of naming Redwood as "contingent payee", CloudCart's procurement asks that the escrow agreement name an independent trustee with instructions to pay Redwood in defined insolvency scenarios. That is a drafting/logistics change we can live with.

2) Refund fallback: CloudCart cannot accept a blanket 30-day recoupment right that would let Redwood withhold payouts unilaterally; willing to accept a 30-day cure period plus an arbitration clause for disputed refunds over $25k.

We can take your annotated redline and incorporate these two points. Call on Monday 7/19 at 9:00 AM PST works for us to finalize language. If you can send the annotated doc and a short summary of the two MSA paragraphs (order form ownership + escrow/fallback), we'll circulate internally and come back with a clean signature-ready order form.

Thanks,
Susan
Director, Commercial Partnerships
CloudCart
